about.short: Ingénieur docteur en électronique, spécialisé en caractérisation de transistors et validation de composants numériques complexes. Expert en testeurs ATE, automatisation (Python, C++) et technologies GaN/SiGe. Conception de cartes électroniques et analyse de fiabilité.
full: Ingénieur docteur en électronique, passionné par les nouvelles technologies et expert en test de produits numériques. J'apporte une solide expertise acquise notamment chez SERMA Technologies et au laboratoire IMS. Spécialisé dans la caractérisation de transistors et la validation de composants numériques complexes, je maîtrise les testeurs numériques (ATE) ainsi que l'automatisation de bancs de test (Python, C++, VBA, IC-CAP).

Ma connaissance approfondie des technologies HEMT GaN, HBT SiGe et MOSFET Si, couplée à mes compétences en conception de cartes électroniques (Altium Designer, KiCad) et ma capacité à évaluer la fiabilité et la robustesse des produits, me permettent d'apporter des solutions complètes et innovantes pour les défis complexes de qualification électronique.

experiences.description: Spécialisée dans la maîtrise des technologies de l’électronique, SERMA Technologies accompagne ses clients dans les phases de R&D, d’ingénierie, de fabrication et de maintenance.

publications.title-long: Evaluation de la robustesse d'une technologie HEMT GaN normally-off à implantation d’ions fluorures co-intégrée avec une technologie HEMT GaN normally-on
publications.title: Robustesse des transistors HEMT GaN normally-off (Thèse)
publications.abstract: Thanks to the outstanding properties of GaN, such as its wide band gap, its high critical electric field, its ability to operate at high temperatures and its high frequency performances, GaN-based HEMTs are considered as the best candidates for the next generation of RF power circuits. Meeting the stringent requirements of 5G, multifunctional GaN MMICs (Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits) have already successfully replaced discrete Si and GaAs circuits in base stations with considerable gains in terms of integration and performances. However, the standard GaN HEMT is normally-on type, which means that it is naturally in conduction mode in the absence of gate polarisation (VGS = 0 V). This is due to the strong spontaneous and piezoelectric polarisation of the material. The lack of technology that co-integrates normally-off and normally-on GaN HEMTs is a considerable disadvantage for many applications in terms of safety, reliability, integration and power consumption. The fabrication of normally-off GaN HEMTs at industrial scale remains a challenge due to the high carrier density in the channel. The aims of this thesis work is to assess the robustness and the performances of normally-off GaN HEMTs fabricated by the fluorine ions implantation technique. These HEMTs are manufactured by adding the required steps to the manufacturing process of a commercial normally-on GaN HEMT technology. They will allow the fabrication of digital circuits for the control of high performances power amplifiers circuits, always based on normally-on GaN HEMTs, due to their higher performance. Studies have been carried out on the first and on the second attempts of the founder to co-integrate normally-on and normally-off GaN HEMTs. Automated measurement procedures and tools were developed to assess devices performances and robustness. DC characterisation campaigns showed the high performances and the low dispersion of the HEMTs of the second batch. The normally-off GaN HEMT provide a truly positive threshold voltage Vth = +0,35 V, a peak transconductance gm,max = 590 mS.mm 1 and a drain current density IDS,max over 1 A.mm-1. Accelerated ageing step-stress tests showed several degradation modes related to the presence of fluorine ions in normally-off GaN HEMTs heterostructure. A negative shift in the voltage Vth of the latter is observed from a drain voltage VDS = 10 V. This shift reaches down to -0,85 V in on-state condition at VGS = 1,5 V and VDS = 18 V. A field-assisted migration mechanism of fluorine ions was proposed to explain the normally-off GaN HEMT degradations. This work contributes to a better understanding of the degradation mechanisms affecting the reliability and the performances of normally-off GaN HEMTs fabricated by the fluorine ion implantation technique.

publications.title: Stabilité de la tension de seuil dans les HEMT GaN
publications.abstract: Abstract: Fluorine ion migration in normally-off AlN/GaN HEMTs fabricated by fluorine ion plasma implantation technology is evidenced. Devices under test are co-integrated into the OMMIC commercial D006GH/D01GH MMIC process, providing fluorine-free normally-on HEMTs. Gate reverse bias step-stress experiment at a drain fixed voltage of 0 V, carried out as well on normally-on ones as on normally-off ones, shows a permanent negative shift in the threshold voltage Vth of normally-off devices only. Vth degradation is starting at a VGS,stress of −8 V, with a negative shift from 0 V to −0.4 V at VGS,stress = −30 V, while the transconductance gm and gm,max remains unchanged prior to breakdown that occurred at VGS,stress ranging between −26 and −32 V. Since the positive threshold voltage of these devices is induced by F-ions dose and position, the above result suggests a possible drift of F-ions away from the 2DEG channel. A field-assisted migration mechanism of fluorine ions is proposed and supported by the absence of Vth degradation in fluorine-free normally-on devices.
